title: Timeline and steps (Earlier / Previously / Later / Eventually)
subtitle: Transitions · 27 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **27 of the official questions in Transitions are this one** — 22 Easy, 5 Medium, 0 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The sentences carry dates, years, or process steps like 'first... then...'.
- The blank sentence moves to a different point in time.
- Most of the choices are time words that point in opposite directions (earlier or later, soon or eventually), plus one or two logic decoys.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Write down the time of each sentence: a year, 'step 1, step 2', or before/after.
- 2) Decide whether the blank sentence jumps backward (earlier, previously), forward (later, subsequently), or to the last step of a process (eventually, finally).
- 3) Pick the time word that matches that direction.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You assume the text runs forward and pick 'next' or 'later' when the blank sentence actually goes back to an earlier date to give background.
Compare the dates themselves, not the order of the sentences.
You also pick a cause word ('as a result') just because one event came after another.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You assume the text runs forward and pick 'next' or 'later' when the blank sentence actually goes back to an earlier date to give background.
Compare the dates themselves, not the order of the sentences.
